Spreadsheet Formatting

We examined 4 spreadsheet files in the repository; 2 have at least one formatting issue.

File Sheet Issue Detail
processed_data_t2_anonym.xlsx Sheet 1 Empty or unnamed columns 10 columns are empty or have a blank header.
processed_data_t1_anonym.xlsx Sheet 1 Empty or unnamed columns 6 columns are empty or have a blank header.

Spreadsheet formatting such as colour, merged cells, and blank rows/columns is not preserved when data are read programmatically or exported to CSV. Store data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable, no colour-encoded meaning) so it is machine-readable.

Careless Responding

No file could be screened for careless responding.

What this does not cover. Only 0 of 4 data files could be screened: the rest had no detectable multi-item scale block, or too few respondents. Even in a screened file, these checks only look at multi-item rating scales — the only place where a repeated or flat answer pattern is interpretable. Single questions, open text, demographics and any item outside a detected scale block are never examined. A respondent can therefore answer most of a survey carelessly and still not be flagged here, and finding nothing is not evidence that a dataset is free of careless responding.

  • 10 installable dependencies detected.

README Files

README files are a way to document the contents and structure of a folder, helping users locate the information they need. You can use a README to document changes to a repository, and explain how files are named. Please consider adding a README to each repository or including ‘README’ in the name of your overview document.

Study/Repository Mismatch

The studies named in the manuscript do not match how the repository’s files are grouped: the manuscript names studies (ex2, ex3) with no matching files in the repository. Check that every study has its own clearly-named folder or file prefix, and that the folder names match how the manuscript refers to each study.

Absolute Paths

Best programming practice is to use relative file paths (e.g., ‘./files’) instead of absolute file paths (e.g., ‘C://Lakens/project_dir/files’) as these folder names do not exist on other computers. No absolute file paths were found in any of the code files.

Working Directory (setwd)

Best programming practice is to avoid setwd() in analysis code: it hardcodes an assumption about the working directory (often an absolute path on the author’s own machine), so the code breaks when run anywhere else. Keep the working directory as the caller sets it and use relative paths. No setwd() calls were found in any of the code files.

Package Installation (install.packages)

Best programming practice is to avoid install.packages() in analysis code: it installs software on whoever runs the script without asking, which is at minimum disruptive (an unexpected install, network access, a package version the author never tested against) and at worst a security risk if it points at an untrusted repository. Document required packages instead (a README, or a list of them: an renv.lock/DESCRIPTION for R, a requirements.txt for Python). No install.packages() calls were found in any of the code files.

Libraries / Imports

Best programming practice is to load all required libraries/imports in one block near the top of the code. In all code files, libraries/imports were loaded in one block.

> make_party_outcome <- function(x, nonvoter_label = character()) {
> 
>   factor(
>     case_when(
>       is.na(x) ~ NA_character_,
>       x %in% nonvoter_label ~ NA_character_,
>       x == "AfD" ~ "AfD",
>       x == "BSW" ~ "BSW",
>       TRUE ~ "Non-populist"
>     ),
>     levels = c("Non-populist", "AfD", "BSW")
>   )
> }
> prepare_party_sample <- function(
>     data,
>     choice_variable,
>     ego_variable,
>     systemic_variable,
>     nonvoter_label = character(),
>     group_sample = FALSE
> ) {
> 
>   prepared <- data %>%
>     filter(eligible_quality)
> 
>   if (group_sample) {
>     prepared <- prepared %>%
>       filter(gr_filter == 1)
>   }
> 
>   prepared %>%
>     mutate(
>       party_outcome = make_party_outcome(
>         .data[[choice_variable]],
>         nonvoter_label = nonvoter_label
>       )
>     ) %>%
>     filter(
>       !is.na(party_outcome),
>       !is.na(.data[[ego_variable]]),
>       !is.na(.data[[systemic_variable]])
>     ) %>%
>     mutate(
>       ego_z = as.numeric(scale(.data[[ego_variable]])),
>       systemic_z = as.numeric(scale(.data[[systemic_variable]]))
>     ) %>%
>     dplyr::select(
>       party_outcome,
>       ego_z,
>       systemic_z
>     )
> }
> fit_party_model <- function(data) {
> 
>   nnet::multinom(
>     party_outcome ~ ego_z + systemic_z,
>     data = data,
>     Hess = TRUE,
>     model = TRUE,
>     trace = FALSE,
>     maxit = 1000
>   )
> }
> tidy_party_model <- function(model, level, outcome, N) {
> 
>   coefficient_matrix <- coef(model)
>   se_matrix <- summary(model)$standard.errors
> 
>   tibble(
>     party = rep(
>       rownames(coefficient_matrix),
>       each = ncol(coefficient_matrix)
>     ),
>     term = rep(
>       colnames(coefficient_matrix),
>       times = nrow(coefficient_matrix)
>     ),
>     b = as.vector(t(coefficient_matrix)),
>     SE = as.vector(t(se_matrix))
>   ) %>%
>     filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
>     mutate(
>       level = level,
>       outcome = outcome,
>       N = N,
>       predictor = case_when(
>         term == "ego_z" ~ "Egocentric victimhood",
>         term == "systemic_z" ~ "Systemic victimhood",
>         TRUE ~ term
>       ),
>       z = b / SE,
>       p = 2 * pnorm(abs(z), lower.tail = FALSE),
>       OR = exp(b),
>       conf.low = exp(b - 1.96 * SE),
>       conf.high = exp(b + 1.96 * SE)
>     ) %>%
>     dplyr::select(
>       level,
>       outcome,
>       party,
>       predictor,
>       N,
>       b,
>       SE,
>       OR,
>       conf.low,
>       conf.high,
>       p
>     )
> }
> compare_afd_bsw_slope <- function(model, term, level, outcome, N) {
> 
>   coefficient_matrix <- coef(model)
>   variance_matrix <- vcov(model)
> 
>   afd_name <- paste0("AfD:", term)
>   bsw_name <- paste0("BSW:", term)
> 
>   afd_index <- match(afd_name, colnames(variance_matrix))
>   bsw_index <- match(bsw_name, colnames(variance_matrix))
> 
>   if (is.na(afd_index) || is.na(bsw_index)) {
>     stop(
>       paste0(
>         "Coefficient names were not found in vcov(model). ",
>         "Inspect colnames(vcov(model)). Expected: ",
>         afd_name,
>         " and ",
>         bsw_name,
>         "."
>       )
>     )
>   }
> 
>   difference <-
>     coefficient_matrix["AfD", term] -
>     coefficient_matrix["BSW", term]
> 
>   variance_difference <-
>     variance_matrix[afd_index, afd_index] +
>     variance_matrix[bsw_index, bsw_index] -
>     2 * variance_matrix[afd_index, bsw_index]
> 
>   SE_difference <- sqrt(variance_difference)
>   z_difference <- difference / SE_difference
>   p_difference <- 2 * pnorm(
>     abs(z_difference),
>     lower.tail = FALSE
>   )
> 
>   tibble(
>     level = level,
>     outcome = outcome,
>     predictor = if_else(
>       term == "ego_z",
>       "Egocentric victimhood",
>       "Systemic victimhood"
>     ),
>     N = N,
>     b_difference = difference,
>     SE_difference = SE_difference,
>     OR_ratio = exp(difference),
>     conf.low = exp(difference - 1.96 * SE_difference),
>     conf.high = exp(difference + 1.96 * SE_difference),
>     p_difference = p_difference
>   )
> }

>     rep("Group-based victimhood", 3)
>   ),
>   outcome = rep(
>     c("Voting intention", "Actual vote", "Donation"),

>     exp_h1_actual_group,
>     exp_h1_donation_group
>   )
> )
> get_forest_results <- function(level, outcome, model) {
> 
>   ci <- suppressMessages(confint(model)) %>%
>     as.data.frame() %>%
>     tibble::rownames_to_column("term") %>%
>     setNames(c("term", "conf.low", "conf.high"))
> 
>   broom::tidy(model) %>%
>     filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
>     left_join(ci, by = "term") %>%
>     transmute(
>       level,
>       outcome,
>       N = nobs(model),
>       victimhood = if_else(
>         str_detect(term, "ego"),
>         "Egocentric victimhood",
>         "Systemic victimhood"
>       ),
>       OR = exp(estimate),
>       conf.low = exp(conf.low),
>       conf.high = exp(conf.high)
>     )
> }
> forest_data <- pmap_dfr(
>   forest_models,
>   get_forest_results
> ) %>%
>   mutate(
>     level = factor(
>       level,
>       levels = c(
>         "Individual-based victimhood",
>         "Group-based victimhood"
>       )
>     ),
>     victimhood = factor(
>       victimhood,
>       levels = c(
>         "Egocentric victimhood",
>         "Systemic victimhood"
>       )
>     ),
>     outcome_order = dplyr::recode(
>       outcome,
>       "Donation" = 1,
>       "Actual vote" = 2,
>       "Voting intention" = 3
>     ),
>     outcome_label = paste0(outcome, "<br>(<i>N</i> = ", N, ")"),
>     outcome_label = forcats::fct_reorder(
>       outcome_label,
>       outcome_order
>     )
>   )
> forest_position <- position_dodge(width = 0.42)
> p_forest <- ggplot(
>   forest_data,
>   aes(
>     x = OR,
>     y = outcome_label,
>     color = victimhood,
>     shape = victimhood,
>     group = victimhood
>   )
> ) +
>   geom_vline(
>     xintercept = 1,
>     linetype = "dashed",
>     linewidth = 0.6,
>     color = "grey35"
>   ) +
>   geom_errorbar(
>     aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high),
>     orientation = "y",
>     position = forest_position,
>     width = 0.16,
>     linewidth = 0.75
>   ) +
>   geom_point(
>     position = forest_position,
>     size = 3.0,
>     stroke = 0.7
>   ) +
>   facet_wrap(
>     ~ level,
>     nrow = 1,
>     scales = "free_y"
>   ) +

Reported vs. reproduced
